title: Operationalizing tagged-canary feedback loop for performance profiles and consumer opt-in
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: We publish Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost) but lack a standard, operational feedback loop that ties small-scale tagged canaries to profile revisions and gives consumers an opt-in path to test new pins before global rollouts. This creates slow detection of profile drift and manual, error-prone rollbacks.

Goal: Define and build an operational pattern that: 1) creates 'tagged' canary releases of new performance profiles (model+quantization+kernel combos) that targeted customers can opt into; 2) captures standardized telemetry (latency P50/P95, throughput, cost/tokens, error rates, quality delta on eval prompt sets); 3) computes a quality/perf delta score against the pinned profile and surfaces automated rollback recommendations and human review triggers; 4) integrates with the publishing flow so profile updates are gated by canary results and an automated rollback window.

Scope: PM ownership for product contract, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan. Works with ENG for telemetry schema and runtimes, DX for opt-in UX, and Research for quality delta evaluation. Deliverables: telemetry contract doc, canary tag spec, opt-in UX mocks, acceptance test harness, playbook for automated rollback thresholds and human escalation.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry schema defined and implemented for latency, throughput, cost-per-token, error-rate, and quality-delta; fields and units documented in Confluence (link).
Tagged canary feature exists: publishing flow can emit a profile with tag 'canary:<id>' and route 0.5-5% traffic from opt-in customers or internal test tenants.
Quality delta calculation implemented and validated on two pilot models: returns scalar in [-1,1] and documented thresholds for regressions and improvements.
Automated rollback recommendation engine returns PASS/FAIL and an evidence bundle (metric diffs and sample outputs) for human review within the console rollouts UI.
Opt-in UX/messaging live in console with ability for customers to join and leave canary pools and view canary metrics for their traffic.
Playbook written: steps for canary monitoring, escalation, rollback, and postmortem; on-call runbook updated.
Pilot completed with 3 internal customers and no more than one rollback in pilot window; learnings documented.
Security and privacy checklist completed for telemetry; no customer PII sent to public telemetry endpoints.
End-to-end tests in CI that simulate canary publishing, traffic routing, metric collection, and rollback decision logic.
